finding: PMMA in low forced flow (1-5 cm/s) displays spherical-shaped flame fronts and non-monotonic spread rates. Quenching occurs at low flow velocities due to radiative cooling rather than thermal starvation.
fire_safety_relevance: Key benchmark for solid polymer flammability in crewed habitats. Reveals low-speed quiescent airflow can either sustain smoldering or cause unexpected radiative extinction.
limitations: Small scale (2 cm x 10 cm samples); does not model structural bulkhead propagation.

investigation: BASS-II Fuel Geometry and Curvature Effects
source_locator: Urban et al., Combustion and Flame 2019, Section 3.2
finding: Cylindrical and curved geometries experience higher oxygen diffusion fluxes per surface area than flat slabs, altering spread rates and delaying extinction in low airflow.
fire_safety_relevance: Directly guides electrical conduit, cable insulation, and rounded interior structural component design for ISS and commercial space stations.
limitations: Laminar flow tunnel only; does not simulate turbulent cabin ventilation draft.

investigation: FLEX Flame Extinction and Cool Flames
source_locator: PSI Investigation Record PSI-69 / Nayagam et al. Combustion and Flame
finding: Discovered quasi-steady low-temperature 'cool flames' burning without visible light after hot flame extinction in microgravity. Quantified gaseous CO2 and N2 suppression limits.
fire_safety_relevance: Critical safety alert: fires in microgravity can continue burning invisibly at 600-800 K after apparent visible extinction, releasing toxic gases without tripping standard optical sensors.
limitations: Isolated droplet combustion; does not directly quantify solid bulk material burn kinetics.

source_locator: PSI Investigation Record PSI-101 / Urban et al. Smoke Aerosol Report
finding: Smoke particles generated in microgravity are significantly larger in mean diameter than terrestrial counterparts because the absence of buoyant updraft allows longer particle coagulation times.
fire_safety_relevance: Direct engineering basis for spacecraft smoke detectors. Terrestrial ionization detectors calibrated for small sub-micron particles suffer false alarms or delayed detection in microgravity.
limitations: Focuses on early pre-ignition pyrolysis smoke rather than mature flaming aerosols.

investigation: SPICE Smoke Point and Soot Radiation
source_locator: PSI Investigation Record PSI-107 / Sunderland et al.
finding: Measured over 526 co-flow laminar flames. Microgravity flames reach the smoke point at much lower fuel velocities and exhibit spherical tips with up to twice the soot radiative cooling of 1g flames.
fire_safety_relevance: Establishes soot radiation feedback models essential for fire propagation simulation and radiative heat load calculations on spacecraft thermal barriers.
limitations: Gaseous burner fuel study; not directly applicable to bulk polymeric structural items without pyrolytic gas conversion.

finding: Thick solid polymers exhibit severe flammability boundary expansion under Exploration Atmospheres (34% O2, 56 kPa), with sustained concurrent flame spread persisting even at reduced total pressures.
fire_safety_relevance: Direct baseline for Artemis Moon and Mars transit habitat safety standards. Demonstrates that elevated O2 environments offset the flame-suppressing benefit of low pressure.

investigation: Concurrent-Flow Flame Spread in Confined Space
source_locator: Li et al., Combustion and Flame 2021, pp. 242-251
finding: Enclosure walls accelerate microgravity flame spread by preventing lateral heat dissipation and channeling induced airflow, generating 1.8x faster flame propagation in narrow ducts.
fire_safety_relevance: Crucial for avionics bays, equipment racks, and ductwork design where fires occur within tight mechanical enclosures.
limitations: Focused on thin cellulosic sheets; thick composite structural panels require separate validation.
